emb_nbg_post_fix.trigger: phase-3 bisection invalidated: the VIPLite wrapper built mis-shaped buffers from the reversed io-query sizes, and the driver retained poisoned state after the crash series
emb_nbg_post_fix.wrapper_bug: vip_query_input/vip_query_output return sizes head-aligned REVERSED (decoder [1,192,1,32] queried as [32,1,192,1,0,0]); edge_wake_viplite.c rebuilt with per-dim reversal (env switches WAKE_VIP_REV/WAKE_VIP_MEM kept for sweeps)
emb_nbg_post_fix.driver_state_confound: after ~20 SIGSEGVs the PRODUCTION GLaDOS decoder NBG also segfaulted at prepare in any standalone process (both wrappers) while serving fine inside edge_server; vipcore state clears only on reboot
emb_nbg_post_fix.positive_control: decoder NBG (/home/orangepi/npu-current/network_binary.nb) prepare OK post-reboot; then the original pegasus int8 embedding NBG (319776 B) prepare OK
emb_nbg_post_fix.latency: int8 wake_vip_run 1.33-1.41 ms/frame vs CPU teacher 20.58 ms; fp16 float-export NBG 20.77 ms (equal to CPU: no speedup on VIP9000NANODI)
emb_nbg_post_fix.quantization_parity: 200 val windows: int8 cos mean 0.9869 (p10 0.9771), max_abs 17.25 on the +/-100 teacher scale; NPU output range [-51.3, 70.9] clips teacher extremes (clipped_frac 1.0)
emb_nbg_post_fix.recalibration_note: [CORRECTED] The AcuityLite recalibrated NBGs were never actually measured: the device parity script used a hardcoded NBG path, and an argv-argument fix was lost with a /tmp wipe (a concurrent agent reboot), so every post-fix parity run silently re-opened the original teacher NBG. nbg_meta.json proves the ranges DID change: recalib input scale 0.354047 vs 0.468131, output range [-54.18, +86.03] vs [-51.3, +70.86]. The original pegasus NBG quantization noise (cos 0.987) stands; the structural-invariance claim is retracted
emb_nbg_post_fix.streaming_ab: 18 eval clips, fresh wake state per clip: CPU (original head, threshold 0.3) 6/8 pos detected, 3/10 prefilter FA; int8 NPU + original head: 4 clips flip pass->FA, 1 flips pass->miss -> not production-safe as-is
emb_nbg_post_fix.npu_matched_head_teacher: head retrained on device-dumped teacher-NPU embeddings (78974 windows, 191 s): self-consistent, but learns quantization noise as positive signal (pass->FA flips persist)
emb_nbg_post_fix.distilled_student_result: student v2 (592K params, Conv/LeakyRelu, standardized targets, bounded output [-4.5, +3.9]): int8 NBG 578320 B; SELF-PARITY cos 0.9980 (p10 0.9962), max_abs 0.49, latency 0.20 ms/frame (103x vs CPU teacher); head retrained on device-dumped student-NPU embeddings (hold recall 0.989 / FA 0.008 @0.3); 48-clip streaming A/B vs the CPU production chain: recall 27/32 vs 26/32 (fixes two CPU misses: 130749-raw 0.874 vs 0.004, 130749-pitch_up300 0.462 vs 0.0), prefilter FA 2/16 vs 3/16 (bg-000 0.20 vs 0.97), chain 3.38 vs 7.31 ms/frame
emb_nbg_post_fix.operational_note: board auto-rebooted (watchdog) during A/B open/close churn; operator attributed that outage to a concurrent agent breaking the network; production usage is resident-open (single open at service start), heavy open/close churn stays a device risk

bisection.device: create_network fails at ioctl VIPDRV_SET_TASK_PROPERTY (container header byte 4 = 0x05 v5 vs pegasus 0x00); byte-4 patch (0x05->0x00, section table identical) -> create_network ok -> prepare SIGSEGV

emb_nbg_runtime_failure.early_probe_failures: MaxPool->Conv(stride-2) and MaxPool->Slice substitutions died at the pegasus quantize stage (TF-backend layout conventions: onnx 1x1 conv weight must be [c_out, c_in, 1, 1]; slice ends must be positive when steps != 1); not needed for the verdict
emb_nbg_runtime_failure.verdict: [CORRECTED 2026-09-09] Superseded: the prepare crashes were wrapper artifacts (reversed io-query sizes) plus poisoned driver state, not graph topology. Post-fix the original NBG prepares and runs; see emb_nbg_post_fix
emb_nbg_runtime_failure.remaining_npu_path: quantization-aware distilled student (bounded output range so int8 cannot clip); head-parity infrastructure exists (device dump + head retrain + streaming A/B)
